newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Commonwealth staff back industrial action.
newsitem.headline: Commonwealth staff back industrial action.

text.p: Commonwealth Bank of Australia staff on Monday backed an industrial campaign if no progress is made on an enterprise bargaining claim.

Staff attending a national stop-work meeting passed a resolution demanding substantial progress in talks over new enterprise bargaining agreements, a Finance Sector Union of Australia spokeswoman said.
The meeting authorised industrial action from August 22 if no progress was made on the agreements, which cover about 32,000 of the bank's 35,000 staff.
The union is seeking a seven percent pay rise over 12 months and said it was concerned at any downgrading of conditions.
The Commonwealth Bank has said it is prepared to consider a pay rise, but wants more flexible workplace agreements.
A Commonwealth spokeswoman said two-thirds of the bank's branches remained open during the stop-work meeting and only about a third of staff attended the meeting.
Further talks between the union and the bank were scheduled for this week, she said.
